outputs.prompt: Use case: sketch-to-render. INPUT 1 is the user's authoritative schematic for CONSTRUCTION and OVERHEAD VIEW. INPUT 2 is an earlier lamp sprite, ONLY a material/style reference. Create one transparent top-down game sprite exactly following the sketch: a VERTICAL fluorescent TUBE on the LEFT, a skinny VERTICAL wall mounting RAIL on the RIGHT, and two short socket BRACKETS at the TOP and BOTTOM joining the tube ends to that rear rail. This is an OPEN wall light. The tube projects out from the wall on the bracket tips and is fully visible FROM ABOVE, with real open TRANSPARENT SPACE between tube and rear rail. Do NOT fill that gap with a panel. Do NOT put a hood or lid above the tube. Do NOT show a big front-facing glass diffuser or ceiling fitting. The back rail's right edge is the edge that sits flush against a vertical wall; the tube is on the left, toward the room. Trace the sketch's simple side-by-side layout faithfully. A complete slender pale glass cylinder, with neutral ice-grey surface and pale blue-white inner core, readable soft cylindrical shading, held by two ivory ceramic end sockets. Grey-ivory narrow enamel rear rail; modest grey metal top/bottom standoffs. Tube about 1.10m long, distance from rear rail to tube about .14m. Orthographic camera straight DOWN at the top of the wall bracket assembly, no camera-facing elevation, no diagonal or 3/4 showroom view. Slightly different replacement lower socket and one local screw handling rub, otherwise maintained practical equipment. Restrained hand-painted semi-realistic 2D hospital horror material style; broad readable forms, no pixel art, no microscopic grunge. One object, long axis vertical, entire unit in frame with transparent margins. The tube itself may look pale luminous, but NO exterior halo, light pool, bloom or floor shadow; runtime Unity lighting supplies the spill. No wall/floor pixels, no text/logos/checkerboard. Genuine RGBA transparency outside the parts, INCLUDING THE OPEN GAP between the rail and tube. Success means the whole tube is visible from above because the brackets hold it out from the wall, as in the user's sketch.
